name: Sylvie Aldahl
languages: Norwegian (her grandmother's, which she uses on stage to sound mysterious and at home to sound like a granddaughter)
equipment: Heavy coat: a long maroon maxi coat with a fake-fur collar, bought for the stage
Pocket revolver: a .32 in her handbag, because she works late on Hennepin Avenue
Black velvet cloth, a hidden clicker, a tin trumpet and a jar of luminous paint (her trade, and she is good at it)
Playing cards: a tarot deck and a pinochle deck
A handbill: MADAME SYLVIE — MESSAGES FROM BEYOND — THE CARDINAL ROOM, HENNEPIN AVE., THURSDAYS
A good dress, black, and boots
In her handbag: her grandmother Signe's photograph of seven men in Sunday clothes at the edge of a coulee, with seven names on the back in pencil and 'the rim, 24 Aug. 1904, after'
Signe's red cotton kerchief, faded pink, wrapped round the photograph
Signe's last letter, written in hospital: 'Never eat the bread in Hollow Fork. Never let them write you in the Book. If you ever have to go, go to Einar first.'
Car: a 1970 Volkswagen Beetle, orange, with a crystal hanging from the mirror
features: The Family Name (Old Family origin: among the old families of a place she is received and told things a stranger would not be, with advantage on Persuasion checks with them; once per scenario she can get an introduction or a meeting with someone of standing without a check; she can recall the reputation and well-known scandal of a prominent local family. In Hollow Fork the name is Aldahl: the family that left, and every old family in town knows exactly who she is)

The Thin Place (Sensitive: she knows when a presence is within 60 ft, though not where or what; she feels cold spots and wrongness first, and the GM tells her the strongest emotion soaked into any room she enters; once per scene she can open herself to the place and the GM gives her one true impression, at the cost of a point of Dread with no save; it never controls anything and is never a spell)
Read the Room (Sensitive: advantage on Insight checks to tell what a person is feeling, and she knows without a check when someone she is speaking with is frightened, grieving or hiding something)

Closer to the Edge (Sensitive, 2nd level: Dread from The Thin Place can't take her past 5; at Dread 3 or higher, The Thin Place gives two impressions, and she can sense where a presence within 60 ft is to within 10 ft)
Gift: Listener (Sensitive, 3rd level: her impressions often come as voices; once per scene she can hear the last words spoken in a place where someone died, as the GM chooses to give them)

The Séance Trade (Medium background: spiritualist circles, performers and grieving families welcome her and she can arrange a séance in any town with a day's notice; she spots another performer's tricks without a check, and the GM tells her when something in a room is not a trick)

personality.traits: I am a performer on and off stage; I make an entrance even into a diner. I read people for a living and I am almost always right. I laugh at the spirit world because for ten years it never laughed back.
personality.ideals: Grieving people deserve comfort, and a good show is a kind of comfort. I never take more from a widow than she can afford.
personality.bonds: My grandmother Signe, who raised me, and who died in August still afraid of a town she left in 1952. My great-uncle Einar in Winona, whom I have not seen since I was six. The voice that came through at the Kenwood séance on 22 August, which was not a trick.
personality.flaws: I have been a fraud for ten years and I am frightened that the one real thing that ever happened to me will turn out to be a trick too. And I am an Aldahl; in Hollow Fork that is a debt.

appearance: Twenty-eight, tall and striking, with long ash-blonde hair, kohl-rimmed grey eyes (Signe's eyes, the old people in Hollow Fork will say), silver rings on every finger, a maroon maxi coat and a voice trained to carry to the back of a supper club.
backstory: Sylvie Aldahl was born in Minneapolis in 1946 to Magnus Aldahl's son and a woman who did not stay, and was raised by her grandparents, Magnus and Signe, who had left Hollow Fork in 1952 with Magnus's brother Einar and their father Knut, after something the family never discussed. She grew up on Signe's stories of a beautiful farm on the rim of a coulee and a town where nobody was ever sick, told with a look Sylvie did not understand. She ran away to a carnival at seventeen, learned cold reading from a mentalist, and has been Madame Sylvie for ten years: séances in Kenwood parlours, a Thursday act at the Cardinal Room on Hennepin Avenue, comfort and a good show. Signe died on 14 August 1974. On 22 August, at a private séance for a widow, the clicker in Sylvie's shoe was still and the trumpet was in her lap and her grandmother's voice came out of her own mouth in Norwegian, and said: 'Sylvie, they never surrendered it. Go home to the Fork, and go to Einar first.' Signe's letter, in her handbag, says the same, and tells her never to eat the bread. (Hook: the family that left. She is of the house of Aldahl by blood and can speak for it at the Cold Hole in hs-scenario-004; Signe's photograph is CLUE 4e.)
